title: Clean up unhandled KeyboardInterrupt traceback when stopping server via Ctrl+C
description: When stopping server.py using CTRL-C, Python dumps an unhandled KeyboardInterrupt stack traceback instead of exiting cleanly with a graceful shutdown message.

plan: Wrap httpd.serve_forever() in try...except (KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit) in server.py, perform clean socket shutdown, and log a friendly exit message.

title: Week 27 report pack in Google Drive folder is not detected/activated upon 'Sync Workspace'
description: Week 27 pack was added to the drive folder. The file is visible in Drive scan, but clicking 'Sync Workspace' leaves the dashboard showing Week 26 instead of updating the live dashboard view to Week 27.
cause:
1. DRIVE_REPORTS in index.html is statically seeded through Week 26.
2. syncGoogleSheet() fetches /api/sync-sheet (which lacked snapshots) and calls checkDriveSyncStatus() but never updates activeTimeMachineWeek or executes activateTimeMachine(getLatestWeekKey()).
3. Header report buttons (#driveReportLink), live status pill (#liveStatusBadge), and Time Machine return banner contained hardcoded Week 26 text instead of dynamically updating to the latest ingested snapshot.
plan:
1. In server.py, include snapshots payload in /api/sync-sheet response.
2. In index.html, update DRIVE_REPORTS to include Week 27 (1HBfI9itx3BER4IRnH9eavBgAsrDGHnmu).
3. In syncGoogleSheet() and initApp(), dynamically sync TIME_MACHINE_SNAPSHOTS from server response and automatically invoke activateTimeMachine(getLatestWeekKey()) to switch the entire dashboard to Week 27.
4. Dynamically update #driveReportLink href/text to always point to the latest week's Drive pack.
5. Write automated reproduction test verifying that syncWorkspace/syncGoogleSheet updates active week to Week 27.

title: 'undefined' displayed instead of week labels in Time Machine modal list
description: In the F-DSE Governance Time Machine modal list, historical weekly snapshot items display 'undefined (31 Jul 2026)', 'undefined (24 Jul 2026)', 'undefined (17 Jul 2026)', 'undefined (10 Jul 2026)', and 'undefined (03 Jul 2026)' instead of proper week names (e.g. 'Week 26', 'Week 25').
cause: In weekly_snapshots.json (and TIME_MACHINE_SNAPSHOTS), historical snapshots w26 through w22 define 'weekLabel' and 'weekNumber' rather than 'week'. In index.html, renderTimeMachineModalList() accesses '${snap.week}', which evaluates to undefined when 'week' is undefined on older snapshots.
plan:
1. In index.html, update renderTimeMachineModalList() (and related snapshot accessors) to robustly resolve week names via `snap.week || snap.weekLabel || ('Week ' + (snap.weekNumber || ''))`.
2. In src/data/weekly_snapshots.json, normalize all snapshot entries to include both 'week' and 'weekLabel'.
3. Add an automated test in tests/test_server.py asserting no undefined labels appear in snapshot modal rendering.

title: Bad text wrapping in Executive Cockpit KPI status pill (ATO-C GATE)

plan: Add 'whitespace-nowrap shrink-0' to all 4 KPI pill wrappers and inner label spans in #execKpisGrid, and harmonize updateAtoGateKpi() to retain 'px-2.5 py-1 text-[11px] whitespace-nowrap shrink-0'.

title: Clicking on Risk Volume or Risk Mitigation (Burndown) graphs in Performance Trends tab does not drill down
description: On the Performance Trends tab (Tab 4), clicking on data points or bars in the Risk Volume (Backlog Timeline) and Risk Mitigation (Burndown Timeline) graphs does not trigger drill-down or time travel navigation.
cause: Chart.js instances for chartBacklogTimeline and chartBurndownTimeline lacked 'interaction: { mode: "index", intersect: false }' and 'events: ["click", "mousemove"]', requiring pixel-perfect clicks on thin lines or points. Additionally, clicking points only triggered a toast rather than opening a rich interactive weekly volume drill-down modal.

1. Configure 'interaction: { mode: "index", intersect: false }' on both Chart.js instances so clicking anywhere in the column slice fires reliably.
2. Implement openTimelineDrilldownModal(weekKey, metrics) presenting the full weekly breakdown of active risks, opened/closed counts, and score averages with a 1-click 'Travel to Week' action.

title: Dashboard UI footer build date not updated (displays stale '2026-08-20 06:02 UTC')
description: build date not updated. Dashboard UI footer in australia-southeast1 still displays 'Release: dev • Build: 2026-08-20 06:02 UTC' even after deploying revision monaro-risk-dash-dev-00005-td5.
cause:
1. HTTP Caching: Neither deploy/nginx.conf nor index.html specifies cache-control headers for data/ or .json files. Browsers aggressively cache data/build_info.json from previous visits (e.g. August 20).
2. Unbusted Fetch in Frontend: src/js/app.js fetches data/build_info.json via a plain fetch('data/build_info.json') without { cache: 'no-store' } or a cache-busting timestamp/query parameter (e.g. ?t=${Date.now()}).
3. Default Fallback in HTML: index.html hardcodes '2026-08-20 15:45 UTC' as default fallback text in the footer span #footerBuildDateVal if the JSON fails to load or isn't parsed.
plan:
1. In src/js/app.js, add cache: 'no-store' and a cache-busting timestamp query parameter to fetch('data/build_info.json?t=' + Date.now(), { cache: 'no-store' }).
2. In deploy/nginx.conf, add a location block for data/ with 'add_header Cache-Control "no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate"; add_header Pragma "no-cache"; add_header Expires 0;'.
3. In index.html, update the hardcoded fallback text in footerBuildDateVal to display 'Checking...' or 'Live' until fetched.
4. Commit, push, and verify that the dashboard footer displays the live UTC build timestamp immediately without requiring manual browser cache clears.

title: Optimize Cloud Build pipeline duration and execution efficiency
description: The build is quite slow (03:27 total duration), even though the app is very simple. Step 1 ('gcr.io/google.com/cloudsdktool/cloud-sdk' checking/creating Artifact Registry) alone takes 01:54 (55% of the total build duration). Additional overhead includes sequential redundant docker pushes, repeating IAM bindings in step 7 (00:26), and pulling heavy cloud-sdk images for simple script tasks. Reference Cloud Logging: https://cloudlogging.app.goo.gl/tsRS5TR3BwKfzQ9x5, Cloud Build ID: 450991c8-f953-4823-90ea-27d3ff2ac2ec.
cause:
1. Step 1 (01:54 / 55% of total time): Pulls heavy multi-GB gcr.io/google.com/cloudsdktool/cloud-sdk image to run redundant describe/create checks on the static Artifact Registry repository 'cloud-run-source-deploy', which is already permanently provisioned.
2. Step 2: Uses cloudsdktool/cloud-sdk for a simple bash script generating data/build_info.json instead of a lightweight runner (e.g. bash or python).
3. Steps 4 & 5: Executes sequential explicit 'docker push' commands despite images already being declared in the top-level 'images:' block, which Cloud Build automatically pushes concurrently.
4. Step 7 (00:26): Runs 6 sequential gcloud CLI IAM and IAP policy binding commands on every commit build, re-applying static access controls that are already codified and provisioned in deploy/provision_environment.sh.
5. Worker Machine Sizing: Omits machineType in options, defaulting to a low-resource worker pool.
plan:
1. Remove redundant Step 1 (Artifact Registry describe/create) from deploy/cloudbuild.yaml since the repository is static infrastructure provisioned by deploy/provision_environment.sh.
2. In Step 2 (metadata injection), switch container image to lightweight 'bash' or integrate into the test step to eliminate cloud-sdk dependency.
3. Remove explicit docker push steps (Steps 4 & 5) and rely on Cloud Build's native concurrent 'images:' upload.
4. Streamline Step 7 IAM/IAP policy re-application: either remove it from the per-commit build path (moving enforcement strictly to deploy/provision_environment.sh) or combine the commands into parallel execution if verification is desired.
5. Add machineType: 'E2_HIGHCPU_8' to options in deploy/cloudbuild.yaml to boost network and CPU throughput.
6. Test build execution via Cloud Build trigger and verify pipeline duration drops under 45 seconds.

title: Scan Drive button is not picking up new files in Google Drive
description: The scan drive button is not picking up new files added to the Google Drive folder. This issue was investigated and patched previously in Bug #85, but has reoccurred.
phase: Scheduled Ingestion Pipeline & Static Sync (Option B)
cause:
1. Static Container Architecture: Cloud Run deploys a pure static Nginx container (deploy/Dockerfile: FROM nginx:alpine) where server.py and Python are not executed. Nginx routes /api/check-drive-sync to index.html (try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html), causing fetch().json() in src/js/app.js to fail silently with a JSON parse error.
2. Silent Exception Swallowing: server.py query_live_drive_folder wraps Drive API calls in a broad 'except Exception: return []', silently masking ADC credential expirations, Drive API permission issues, or network failures, and falling back to a static list.
3. Incomplete Bug #85 Resolution: Bug #85 was artificially mitigated by hardcoding Week 29 into server.py DEFAULT_DRIVE_REPORTS and mocking the API in unit tests, rather than establishing an automated ingestion pipeline in CI/CD.
plan:
Option B Implementation Plan (Scheduled Ingestion Pipeline & Static Sync):
1. Automated Ingestion Script: Implement scripts/sync_drive.py (or enhance scripts/pipeline.py) using the Google Drive API and ADC/Service Account to scan the Monaro reporting folder (1JIsbi35mXn4W-NxjbLTWo22FQMv_zv-C), extract metadata for new weekly packs (e.g. Week 30+), update data/monaro/snapshots.json and config.json, and register all discovered reports.
2. Cloud Build & Scheduled Ingestion Hook: Integrate scripts/sync_drive.py into deploy/cloudbuild.yaml (using the existing lightweight python:3.13-slim runner) so that each build/deploy automatically pulls the latest Google Drive files into the deployed container, and configure a scheduled trigger for regular automated synchronization.
3. Frontend Static Hosting Awareness: In src/js/app.js (checkDriveSyncStatus), add graceful handling when running under static hosting: if /api/check-drive-sync returns HTML or 404, fall back cleanly to reading data/monaro/snapshots.json with cache-busting, display the latest ingested snapshot report in the modal, and present an informative status badge ('Synced via CI/CD Pipeline') with clear feedback instead of an unhandled JSON parse error.
4. Eliminate Hardcoded Weekly Fallbacks: Deprecate manual additions to server.py DEFAULT_DRIVE_REPORTS; ensure snapshots and known reports are derived dynamically from data/monaro/snapshots.json.
5. Automated Verification: Add automated unit and regression tests verifying sync_drive.py detection logic and frontend graceful fallback behavior.

If identical, show clear informational toast: '✓ Already up to date: No new reports found (Latest: Week {N})'.

3. In server.py (handle_sync), implement in-flight mutex lock so multiple concurrent syncs are blocked, returning status 'in_progress' if already running, and explicit 'updated: true/false' with human-readable summary.

title: Playback unavailable for podcast in Time Machine
description: When viewing a historical snapshot in Time Machine (e.g. Week 25 - 24 Jul 2026 on Project Monaro Executive Summary), the NotebookLM Podcast audio widget displays 'Playback unavailable' and disables the Download Audio button.
repro_test: tests/frontend/dashboard_ux.test.js::handles historical snapshot podcast audio fallback without audio file (Bug #112)
cause:
1. Snapshot Metadata Ignored by Audio Resolver: In data/monaro/snapshots.json, historical snapshots (e.g. w25, w24, w23, w22, w21, w10, w4) explicitly specify "hasAudio": false while keeping a placeholder "audioFile": "assets/podcast_w25.mp3". However, resolvePodcastAudioSrc(weekKey, snap) in src/js/app.js (lines 1693-1706) ignores snap.hasAudio === false and unconditionally returns snap.audioFile ("assets/podcast_w25.mp3").
2. Relative vs. Absolute URL Cache Key Mismatch: When updatePodcastAudioForWeek('w25') runs, audioEl.onerror sets PODCAST_AUDIO_CACHE["assets/podcast_w25.mp3"] = false and calls setAudioUnavailable(), which removes the src attribute without calling audioEl.load() (leaving audioEl.currentSrc as the full URL "http://localhost:9000/assets/podcast_w25.mp3" in Chrome), while keeping the Play button (▶) enabled because snap.podcastScript is present.
3. Failed HTML5 Audio Play Without Speech Fallback: When the user clicks Play (togglePodcastPlayback(), lines 1159-1225), src resolves to the absolute URL "http://localhost:9000/assets/podcast_w25.mp3" (or re-binds "assets/podcast_w25.mp3"). Because PODCAST_AUDIO_CACHE[src] looks up the full URL instead of the relative key (evaluating to undefined !== false), togglePodcastPlayback() bypasses the Web Speech API fallback (playPodcastFromIndex(0)) and calls audioEl.play() on the 404 audio resource, which rejects and sets #podcastTimeLabel to 'Playback unavailable' (line 1222).
plan:
1. Respect snap.hasAudio in resolvePodcastAudioSrc & updatePodcastAudioForWeek (src/js/app.js): If snap.hasAudio === false (and no valid audioSizeBytes/audioDurationSeconds exists), return null from resolvePodcastAudioSrc() or immediately invoke setAudioUnavailable() without probing a non-existent 404 MP3 path.
2. Normalize PODCAST_AUDIO_CACHE Keys & Clear Audio State: Normalize cache keys across relative and absolute URLs, and call audioEl.load() after removing src in setAudioUnavailable() so audioEl.currentSrc is cleared.
3. Seamless Speech Synthesis Fallback in togglePodcastPlayback(): In togglePodcastPlayback() (and inside the audioEl.play().catch() handler on line 1218), if studio MP3 playback fails or is unavailable for a historical snapshot that has a valid snap.podcastScript, automatically fall back to playPodcastFromIndex(0) (Web Speech Synthesis of Alex & Jordan's dialogue) rather than halting with 'Playback unavailable'.
4. Synthesize / Backfill Missing Historical Podcast Audio Assets: Run scripts/check_podcast_status.py --fix (or pipeline audio synthesis) to generate studio MP3 files (podcast_w*.mp3) in GCS / data/monaro/ for historical snapshots where studio audio is desired.
5. Add Automated Regression Test: Add a unit test in Vitest (dashboard_ux.test.js) and pytest verifying Time Machine navigation to a snapshot with hasAudio: false cleanly engages transcript/speech fallback and never displays 'Playback unavailable'.

title: Prevent DOM ID mismatch and silent failures by enforcing AST static scan and strict DOM contract across all modules

2. Fail-Fast Migration: Refactor all module renderers to use getRequiredElement(DOM_IDS.<KEY>, '<Context>') so missing elements throw/log immediately.
3. AST Linter / Contract Test: Add an automated test in tests/frontend/dashboard_ux.test.js (and test_frontend_contracts.py) that parses AST of all JS files and asserts that 100% of queried ID literals exist in index.html, preventing regressions in CI.
